title: Andy Campion’s Unrivaled Approach to Youth Sports

summary:
Investors have poured money into youth sports in recent years, with some reports saying the industry is worth as much as $40 billion. It’s no surprise, then, that renowned investors David Blitzer and Josh Harris partnered with The Chernin Group in 2024 to start Unrivaled Sports, a growing portfolio of youth sports investments across baseball, softball, flag football, and more. Unrivaled’s chairman and CEO Andy Campion says they’re only just getting started. 

In this episode of The Deal, Andy tells Alex Rodriguez and Jason Kelly why he left Nike to go all in on youth sports. From the sidelines of a youth baseball tournament at Cooperstown All-Star Village, he explains the business model making youth sports more accessible while also offering premier experiences. 

You can also watch this interview on the Bloomberg Podcasts YouTube page.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How the Iranian Economy Actually Works
title_cn: 伊朗经济实际上是如何运作的
summary: After the Iranian Revolution of 1979, the country's new leaders — religious and political — promised to redistribute the country's wealth and made moves to make Iran independent from western influence and business interests. In the decades since, Iran's economy completely transformed, and it is closer to what Yeganeh Torbati and Bozorgmehr Sharafedin describe as a "mafia state," where fealty to various factions is baked into the country's political economy. In their new book Stolen Revolution: Betrayal and Hope in Modern Iran they trace the massive changes Iran's political economy has undergone since the revolution, and they speak to us today about this history, how average Iranians navigate everyday cronyism, how Iranian leaders treated the country's burgeoning tech sector, and why the recent peace talks might not change all that much about how the country's economy currently operates. (Source: Bloomberg)

summary: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) says maintaining sanctions and a blockade on Iran will be "painful" for Americans ahead of the midterms, but argues that sustaining the pressure for several more months may be the most effective way to move Tehran. Former Republican Senator Jeff Flake says the standoff over Todd Blanche's attorney general nomination shows the limits of President Trump's influence over the Senate.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Jamie McDonald Sworn In as Top Federal Prosecutor on Wall Street
title_cn: 杰米·麦克唐纳 (Jamie McDonald) 宣誓就任华尔街最高联邦检察官
summary: Jamie McDonald, an experienced white-collar lawyer whose clients have included President Donald Trump, was appointed as US Attorney of the Southern District of New York by the judges of the Manhattan-based federal court.

title: Fmr. Sen. Flake: Blanche Fight Shows Limits of Trump's Power
title_cn: 先生。参议员弗雷克：布兰奇之战显示了特朗普权力的局限性
summary: Former Republican Senator Jeff Flake says the standoff over Todd Blanche's attorney general nomination shows the limits of President Trump's influence over the Senate. He predicts Republicans will retain the Senate but lose the House in November, saying divided government could produce more resistance to Trump and a "more normal Washington." The former US ambassador to Turkey also says Ankara should be allowed to rejoin the F-35 program, but only after it gives up possession of Russia's S-400 missile system. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Sen. Kennedy: Iran Pressure Campaign Will Be 'Painful'
title_cn: 肯尼迪参议员：向伊朗施压将是“痛苦的”
summary: Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) says maintaining sanctions and a blockade on Iran will be "painful" for Americans ahead of the midterms, but argues that sustaining the pressure for several more months may be the most effective way to move Tehran. The Louisiana Republican calls inflation "pernicious" and says the Federal Reserve will have to raise rates if it is not brought under control. Sen. Kennedy also says that, "if I had to bet," the Senate Judiciary Committee will not vote on Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general tomorrow. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
